title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: users can upload local and OneDrive files to custom engine agents
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents automation for the tenant-wide User access setting, which the briefing reports as undocumented. Microsoft also documents a general Copilot file-upload policy, so the assertion that no tenant-wide upload switch is documented must be narrowed. The roadmap facts and the principal agent-blocking controls are supported.

claims.quote: These resources also support remediation and applyOnce. ... useraccess resource type ... valueObject | Write | AgentUserAccessValueObject | Configures who can access agents and plugins.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].api with graph call 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors', docs https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta. Add to the existing note: 'Preview automation can apply a tenant-wide all-users or no-users baseline: set mode to applyOnce and baseline.resources to resourceType microsoft.agent.useraccess, resourceVersion 1, with properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory set to everyone or noOne. The calling app needs delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All; the TCM service principal needs delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite, and the signed-in user needs AI Administrator. This reference does not document specific-user/group assignment.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-remediation-applyonce-resources. Keep the preview and non-production qualification.
